corrections.source_says: Set core to no and criterion_3_outcome_scored_on_output to not_met under the supplied codebook. Emails are scored for cultural communication style and overlap with their supplied AI draft, not creativity, novelty, usefulness, or similarity/diversity among different people's outputs. Scoring any feature of an output does not satisfy criterion 3. Keep criterion_2 as met and context_class as none; criterion_1 remains unclear for the AI-order comparison, while the no-AI comparison is fixed before/after. The claimed short-form routing rule is not in the supplied form-spec or codebook, and no qualifying randomized creativity/diversity study is established.

confirmed: Read the complete markdown conversion, including Appendices A-H, and checked the local PDF. The document is arXiv:2609.26403v1, dated 22 Sep 2026, with 17 PDF pages; source.version, title and author list match the document (PDF p. 1; PDF page count).

Appendices A-H occupy PDF pp. 11-16; p. 17 contains only a running header. Table 3 separately refers to supplemental full example emails without giving a location (PDF p. 8, Table 3). The form correctly distinguishes that missing supplement from the included appendices.

One online human study uses a mixed design with cultural group between people and assistance condition within people. No-AI is always Task 1; low- and high-context AI drafts occupy Tasks 2 and 3 under a Latin-square/counterbalancing schedule, with no explicit statement of random assignment (PDF pp. 3-4, Section 3.2; p. 13, Table 5).

The analyzed sample is 175 people: 89 American and 86 Japanese participants. The same people contribute to each condition, so the repeated arm counts must not be added as independent participants; this is not an experiment with fewer than 50 analyzed people (PDF p. 2, Introduction; pp. 6-7, Figures 4-6; p. 13, Table 4; p. 15, Appendix H).

The paper reports 257 recruited in Section 3.5 and 228 in the draft-generation analysis without reconciling those totals; the form correctly flags this source inconsistency and leaves randomized counts null (PDF p. 5, Sections 3.5 and 4; p. 6, Figure 3).

The dataset announcement counts 771 emails, including 474 American and 297 Japanese emails, not participants or the final analytical sample. No explicit total of analyzed output observations is printed for the change-score model, so its n_units need not be inferred (PDF p. 2, Preregistration and Dataset; p. 6, Section 4.2).

All numbers in the reported string and one_line_finding match: low-context descriptive mean change M = -2.09 and high-context M = +2.60 markers per 100 words; adjusted low-versus-high beta = -4.75, SE = 0.19, z = -25.71, p < .001. Figure 5 identifies its means as descriptive and its error bars as 95% CIs, without printing numerical interval bounds (PDF p. 7, Section 4.2 and Figure 5).

The outcome is the sum of indirectness and imposition-mitigation marker counts normalized per 100 words. A single bilingual coder counted markers, and the change-score model uses a random intercept per participant; these are raw communication-style units, not standardized creativity effects (PDF pp. 4-5, Section 3.4.1; p. 6, Section 4.2).

AI reliance compares a submitted email with its supplied AI draft, using retained draft words divided by final-email words; it does not compare different participants' emails. Post-task preference responses concern perceived naturalness (PDF p. 5, Section 3.4.2; pp. 14-15, Appendix G; pp. 15-16, Appendix H and Table 10).

The named draft-generation models are GPT-5.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Gemini 2.5 Flash; the same scenario/condition supplies identical pre-generated drafts to participants, who may edit or ignore them (PDF p. 4, Section 3.3; pp. 12-14, Appendices D-E).

This is not a synthesis, so study-pooling counts, pooled effects and intervals are inapplicable. The context_class of none is appropriate under the supplied creativity/diversity outcome definition; quasi_people describes the fixed-baseline design but does not establish an in-scope observational outcome (PDF pp. 3-8, Methods and Results; creativity-codebook.md, Sections 1, 3 and 6).

The linked AsPredicted preregistration was additionally read as public HTML at https://aspredicted.org/2jy53q.pdf, with no file saved. It confirms the always-first no-AI baseline, counterbalanced AI order and primary communication-score analysis; its conditions item does not explicitly state random allocation (public registration items 3-5; link in PDF p. 2).
summary: The 175 analyzed participants and all statistics in the reported result and one-line finding match the PDF, but preregistration, exclusions and several classification fields need correction. The fixed-baseline, counterbalanced study reports no explicit random assignment and measures email style and draft retention rather than creativity or diversity across writers, so core eligibility should be no.
